svg.title: rondOfeed wiring layout
svg.text: Top view, rear wall at the top. Both drawings have the same orientation. Board on a 2.54 mm grid, mounting holes as given by Adafruit and GeeekPi.
To scale. Plate, disc and lid removed. Dashed: the GeeekPi Half-Size board (outline assumed) and its 4 corner holes.
Adafruit, component side, 30 rows, 51 × 81 mm. Columns A–E and F–J are separate. Rails are not connected to each other.
• Proposal, not built or tested. Check it against your parts before soldering.

• Board: Adafruit Perma-Proto Half-Size as drawn, or GeeekPi Half-Size. The carrier has posts for both. GeeekPi: drill its 4 corner holes to 3.2 mm for the M3 screws, and check that its rows and rails match this drawing.
• Breakout: one 10-pin header in F16–F25. The terminal pins line up with holes A18–A23. Solder them if they reach, for support. Leave A18–E23 empty.
• Put a spacer under the terminal edge if those pins do not reach. The terminal screws press on an otherwise one-sided mount.
• Fit the jumpers, R1 to R3 and D1 first. Column G is half under the breakout. The ground link crosses row 14 on top of the board, so use insulated wire.
• INDEX and UART stay unconnected. Bend the C1 leads to fit the rail spacing.
• Converter shown as a 3-pin in-line module, 11.5 × 7.5 mm (example: R-78E5.0-0.5). Check its pin order. It sits flipped: IN in row 30.
• Light barrier: R2 feeds the IR LED from 3V3 (about 20 mA), R3 pulls GP6 up. The long leg of the LED is the anode. Check the collector leg in the phototransistor's datasheet.
• The 12 V feed runs round the rear corner of the board, clear of the M3 screw in row 30.
• GP2 to GP6 are on the wall side of the Pico, so those wires go round the left side of the board. Keep them away from the antenna at the front end of the Pico.
